doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

chapter: Career as a leader and teaching
title: Her recording career and management
summary: She records about one album a year since 1975, has a new contract and a manager, and finds things easier with grown children.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You’ve had pretty good success it seems with your recording career. Is it a challenge? Is it difficult to get records out and has it changed over the years?

Well I have a contract now so we’ve done four and we’re — I don’t know how many more we’ll do. It’s a long deal so probably there’ll be a lot more coming out. But if I look back over the ones as a leader that I’ve done I do on average one a year. Because I think I started in 1975, so there’s about 25 out. That’s the average. That’s the way it works out. There’s more than one some years, and—
Do you do your own business, I guess, pretty much?

Well I have a manager. You know I work with people and yeah, I get some help. Because you know when you’re touring it’s too hard, even with the — well I have to get a palm pilot, that’s what I think, so I can get the e-mail. I don’t have that yet. I just got a new computer. But even at that it’s a little difficult sometimes to keep up with things. You let too many things slide that you really want to do. So it’s good to have some people supporting you.
Is it somewhat easier now that your kids are grown?
Oh yeah. Of course, yes. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
